newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania lifts restrictions on press.
newsitem.headline: Albania lifts restrictions on press.

text.p: The Albanian parliament approved a measure on Wednesday lifting press restrictions that an emergency all-party government had introduced last month during the height of the country's period of lawless mayhem.
The emergency press restriction measure had required all Albanian newspapers to submit articles in advance of publication to government-appointed committees for their approval.

Most Albanian newspapers had already suspended publication prior to the measure, which was passed on March 2, because of the anarchy that was sweeping the country following the collapse of fraudulent get-rich-quick investment schemes.

There are currently three daily newspapers publishing in Albania: Rilindja Demokratiki (Democratic Renaissance), published by the Democratic party, Ziri i Popullit (Voice of the People), published by the Socialist party, and Republika, published by the Republican party.
The country's largest daily, Koha Joni (Our Time), suspended publication indefinitely after its offices were destroyed by a fire last month.
A second independent daily newspaper, Dita Informaction, had its first edition in a month on Tuesday but failed to appear on Wednesday.
The paper's publisher, Shpetim Nazarko, said unknown assailants had shot at his house on Tuesday but no one had been injured.
Nazarko told Reuters several gunmen shot wildly at his house in a Tirana suburb in the early afternoon on Tuesday. He said he did not know the reasons for the attack.
The English-language Albanian Daily News said Nazarko's newspaper had published an article on Tuesday critical of Berisha.
